items.summary: Calibration release: the package's no-shipped-coefficients policy finally comes with the tool that closes the loop. Every shipped set carries the caveat that lever arms depend on material, mode pair, excitation and substrate; calibrate_lever_arms turns reference measurements you control -- a strain-stage sweep, a gated sweep, any points with known (strain, density) -- into your own fitted coefficient matrix, with uncertainties and provenance. New in ramansep.calibration calibrate_lever_arms : weighted least-squares fit of the (m, 2) lever-arm matrix, one linear problem per mode on the shared reference design. With shift sigmas the parameter covariance is the exact known-noise Gauss-Markov result and a per-mode chi-square consistency check comes back with it; without sigmas the covariance uses the residual variance, which is why that path refuses fewer than three reference points instead of inventing an error bar. Identifiability refused, not fudged : reference states collinear in the (strain, density) plane (a strain-only sweep, or gating that strains proportionally) cannot separately determine the two arms of any mode -- the fit raises with an explanation instead of returning one of infinitely many minimizers. CalibrationResult.coefficients() packages a two-mode calibration as a ModeCoefficients with a MANDATORY provenance string; result.K feeds MultiModeModel directly for m > 2. Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated) Noise-free shifts from a known matrix are recovered to machine precision, with zero estimated uncertainty. The hand-built normal-equation solution agrees with an independent QR solve ( numpy.linalg.lstsq on the whitened system) to 1e-10. The orthogonal unit design {(1,0), (0,1)} with unit sigmas has EXACTLY the identity parameter covariance -- the closed form, not an approximation. Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted arms matches the reported sigmas. Degenerate and malformed reference sets raise (collinear designs, n = 1, n = 2 without sigmas, non-positive sigmas, non-finite shifts). The full round trip -- calibrate on synthetic references, package the coefficients, invert forward-generated maps through SeparationModel -- returns the input strain and density maps to 1e-10. 50 tests across Python 3.9-3.13. Install: pip install -U ramansep .

items.summary: Automated risk decisions increasingly depend on probabilistic assessments transmitted across organisational and computational boundaries. A probability estimate may remain numerically intact while losing the contextual information required to evaluate its evidentiary dependence — a condition we term Provenance Loss . We introduce Orphaned Inference — a probabilistic output P ( H | E ) that propagates downstream after its contextual qualification is stripped at a transmission boundary — and show that when downstream agents continue scalar-posterior updating using marginal likelihood ratios, the resulting propagation is equivalent to a Na ̈ıve-Bayes-style independence approximation over the correlated evidence sequence. This double-counts the shared environmental signal, producing Directional Context Amplification , quantified by the Cumulative Provenance Amplification (CPA n ) metric. Under environmental context drift ( C 0 → C 1 ), accumulated phantom certainty persists into the post-shift regime as Post-Shift Epistemic Persistence , driving the mean absolute posterior error close to 1 in true-negative states ( H = 0) during the pre-shift period. In risk-analysis terms, provenance loss separates the numerical value of a risk estimate from the evidentiary conditions under which it remains decision-valid: downstream decision makers may receive an apparently precise probability whose effective evidentiary weight is substantially overstated. A Monte Carlo simulation ( N = 5 , 000 trials, n = 15 agent chain) demonstrates the predicted cascade under the specified parameter regime and documents monotone growth of CPA n across sampled correlation values ρ ∈ { 0 , . . . , 0 . 8 } . We propose three provenance-aware risk-control safeguards and discuss their governance trade-offs.
items.title: Orphaned Inferences in Automated Risk Hierarchies: Na ̈ıve Bayes Amplification under Provenance Loss

items.summary: This reproducibility package accompanies a measurement-science workflow for temporal light modulation (TLM) metric reproduction and computational sensitivity analysis. Five independent MK350S Premium optical waveform records form the bounded commercial demonstration. MetTLM W1–W20 public references support source-traceable PstLM/SVM calculation-pipeline reproduction and sampling-rate, duration and deterministic modelled-effect sensitivity analyses. Evidence identity is preserved so that public waveforms, resampled/windowed/perturbed rows and auxiliary electrical/photometric records are not treated as additional commercial observations. Raw third-party public-reference assets and manufacturer documents are intentionally not redistributed; original DOI/license/checksum provenance and reconstruction scripts are provided instead. items.summary: This record contains the publication-facing verification materials and reproducible Lean 4 certificate packages for the continuing formal validation of the Chronos Navier-Stokes program, extending the original unified clock milestone through certificate versions v1.2–v1.10. The formal development is compiled against OpenAI's public NavierStokesAndEuler repository at the pinned upstream commit using Lean 4.34.0-rc2. It begins from OpenAI's actual selected periodic Navier-Stokes candidate and extends the previously verified Chronos change, arrow, action, and aim clock into a broader temporal-field framework. The formally verified development now includes the closed temporal-exchange balance, the Chronos selector value, an exact selector-defined temporal carrier satisfying, temporal diffusion and relaxation dynamics, a nonnegative temporal-field arrow under the stated sign conditions, an independent change-arrow-aim clock for the temporal carrier, and complete oriented temporal histories including the initial endpoint. The later certificates introduce a general temporal source-law interface and formally analyze a nonlinear radial saturation source law of the form The verified results include its exact energy/action decomposition, nonlinear saturation contribution, nonnegative net arrow under the stated parameter conditions, closed instantaneous and historical clock identities, and an exact necessary-and-sufficient calibration criterion. The calibration theorem separates source identification into zero-state compatibility, directional alignment, and scalar magnitude. The formal development also proves a parameter-free transverse alignment condition and establishes that the radial law depends on the difference between drive and damping rather than identifying those two parameters independently. Taken together, versions v1.2–v1.10 extend the Chronos formal program from a verified Navier-Stokes clock decomposition into a formally connected temporal exchange, selector, carrier, field-dynamics, source-law, and calibration architecture. The uploaded certificate archives contain Lean source modules, reproduction scripts, SHA-256 checksums, build logs, provenance information, and dedicated axiom-audit results. The certificate series was reproduced in the pinned Lean/OpenAI environment with no sorry, admit, or sorryAx dependencies in the audited Chronos declarations.
items.title: Lean-Verified Chronos Physics Framework: Temporal Carrier, Source Law, and Formal Calibration — Milestone 3

items.summary: his work studies the basin geometry of the negative integer Collatz map. Under exact iteration of T(n)={n/2,n even,3n+1,n odd,T(n)= \begin{cases} n/2, & n \text{ even},\\ 3n+1, & n \text{ odd}, \end{cases} the first 10710^7 negative integers are observed to enter one of the three classical negative cycles through −1-1 , −5-5 , and −17-17 . The corresponding empirical basin proportions stabilize near 0.327:0.324:0.3480.327:0.324:0.348 , with a persistent modest excess for the C−17C_{-17} basin. The paper then examines the structure behind these basin frequencies. Basin membership is found to be weakly predicted by simple residue classes modulo 2k2^k , and short prefixes of the 22 -adic valuation itinerary under the accelerated odd Collatz map show essentially no transferable predictive power in held-out tests. A markedly different structure appears in the reverse dynamics. Monotone inverse trees rooted in the three negative attractors show strongly unequal relative sizes, stabilizing near 0.293:0.218:0.4890.293:0.218:0.489 . The associated tree-count ratios remain highly stable over repeated increases in the magnitude cutoff, motivating a common reverse-growth conjecture with basin-dependent amplitudes. Forward trajectories partially erase this reverse-tree asymmetry. Low-reversal trajectories are strongly enriched for the C−17C_{-17} attractor, while increasing non-monotone trajectory complexity attenuates that advantage and moves the observed basin shares closer to the near-balanced global census. The resulting empirical picture is that asymmetric reverse accessibility and forward trajectory mixing jointly shape the macroscopic basin distribution. The paper proposes corresponding conjectures on negative basin densities and reverse-tree ratio convergence. These computations do not prove that every negative integer enters one of the three known cycles, do not exclude additional negative cycles or divergent orbits, and do not resolve the positive Collatz conjecture. The contribution is a computational study of basin structure, reverse accessibility, and mixing in the signed integer extension of the Collatz map.
items.title: Negative-Basin Geometry in the Integer Collatz Map: Forward Census, Reverse-Tree Asymmetry, and Mixing

The corresponding empirical basin proportions stabilize near 0.327:0.324:0.3480.327:0.324:0.348 , with a persistent modest excess for the C−17C_{-17} basin. The paper then examines the structure behind these basin frequencies. Basin membership is found to be weakly predicted by simple residue classes modulo 2k2^k , and short prefixes of the 22 -adic valuation itinerary under the accelerated odd Collatz map show essentially no transferable predictive power in held-out tests. A markedly different structure appears in the reverse dynamics. Monotone inverse trees rooted in the three negative attractors show strongly unequal relative sizes, stabilizing near 0.293:0.218:0.4890.293:0.218:0.489 . The associated tree-count ratios remain highly stable over repeated increases in the magnitude cutoff, motivating a common reverse-growth conjecture with basin-dependent amplitudes. Forward trajectories partially erase this reverse-tree asymmetry. Low-reversal trajectories are strongly enriched for the C−17C_{-17} attractor, while increasing non-monotone trajectory complexity attenuates that advantage and moves the observed basin shares closer to the near-balanced global census. The resulting empirical picture is that asymmetric reverse accessibility and forward trajectory mixing jointly shape the macroscopic basin distribution. The paper proposes corresponding conjectures on negative basin densities and reverse-tree ratio convergence. These computations do not prove that every negative integer enters one of the three known cycles, do not exclude additional negative cycles or divergent orbits, and do not resolve the positive Collatz conjecture. The contribution is a computational study of basin structure, reverse accessibility, and mixing in the signed integer extension of the Collatz map.
items.title: Negative-Basin Geometry in the Integer Collatz Map: Forward Census, Reverse-Tree Asymmetry, and Mixing

items.summary: We study explicit algebraic cycles and the recovery of their supports in three special fourfold settings. For a smooth diagonal intersection of five quadrics in P⁹, a paired splitting plane in the associated ten-hyperplane arrangement produces an orbit of thirty-two degree-four del Pezzo surfaces. Their alternating rational cycle w has square 3. An elliptic-quartic net gives an actual correspondence D = w × η to P² and the Chow projector w × w/3. The paired incidence is smooth of dimension twelve, finite and locally immersed over the sixteen-dimensional diagonal moduli space, and has a nonempty non-evaluation open. Its tangent quotient is an Artinian reduction of the Segre ring of P² × P², with Hilbert function (1, 4, 1). We use this quotient and the relative cycles to identify the complete marked Hodge germ with the paired incidence branch, including its scheme structure. At a very general paired point, the full-character rational Hodge sector is exactly ℚw; the proper characters give the rational Hodge conjecture for these very general fourfolds. The germ statement concerns diagonal deformations. For hypersurface fourfolds of degree d ≥ 5, we prove a reverse recognition theorem. A tangent-exhausting integrated Hodge family with a persistent embedded connected-sum annihilator forces its two candidate ambient planes to lie on the hypersurface and recovers the full rationally weighted primitive class. The conormal variation is surjective onto the true graded ideal-deformation space and has a seventeen-dimensional kernel. An explicit smooth family shows that the equation can nevertheless fail to belong to the square of its Hodge annihilator. Finally, from Paranjape's K3–Prym correspondence we construct a quadratic trace and an explicit sheared odd correspondence, purify it by rational endomorphism selectors, and compute its full and primitive kernels under a stated full Hodge-group hypothesis. Weil-class algebraicity is already known; this part concerns an explicit realization and its action. Further constructions record exact Chow returns and several rigidity phenomena. All genericity restrictions and the distinction between Chow identities, complex Hodge dimensions, and rational Hodge spaces are retained.
items.title: Explicit Hodge Classes and Support Recognition on Special Fourfolds

items.summary: This dataset provides raw LC-MS data files (instrument .raw format) from an untargeted lipidomics analysis of mouse liver, intended as a demonstration dataset for LipiRich (website: https://lipirich.sarahehancock.com , github: https://github.com/sarahehancock/LipiRich ), an open-source Shiny application for normalisation, statistical analysis, and visualisation of untargeted lipidomics data exported from MS-DIAL 5. Sample origin: Liver tissue was obtained from C57BL/6J mice from three dietary groups (n = 8 per group): standard chow, lard-based high-fat diet (45% of energy from fat; 88% lard, 12% safflower oil), and a high-fat diet in which 90% of the lard was substituted with fish oil. Animals and diets are as described in Liu et al. (2014), Scientific Reports 4:5538 ( https://doi.org/10.1038/srep05538 ), from which these liver samples were retained. Lipid extraction: Lipids were extracted from liver tissue (~20 mg) using a modified methyl-tert-butyl ether (MTBE) method. Tissue was homogenized in ice-cold 150 mM ammonium acetate (10 mg tissue/100 μL) using a bead homogenizer, kept below 4°C. Aliquots of homogenate (1 mg equivalent) were added to MTBE:methanol (3:1 v/v, 0.01% BHT) together with a mixed internal standard solution (100 pmol each of PC 17:0/17:0, PE 17:0/17:0, PS 17:0/17:0, PG 17:0/17:0, PA 17:0/17:0 LPC 17:0, LPE 14:0, ceramide d18:1/17:0, dihydrosphingomyelin d18:0/12:0, DAG 15:0/15:0, d-TAG 48:0, and CE 22:1; 10 pmol each d3-palmitoyl carnitine, lactosylceramide 12:0 and glucosylceramide 15:0; 1 nmol cholesterol-d7, 50 pmol PI 15:0_18:1-d7, and 5 pmol N-acylethanolamine 17:1). Samples were rotated at 4°C overnight, then one volume of ice-cold 150 mM ammonium acetate was added, vortexed, and centrifuged to separate phases. The upper organic phase was dried under nitrogen at 37°C and reconstituted in 200 μL chloroform:methanol:water (60:30:4.5 v/v/v; 200 μL) prior to analysis. LC-MS acquisition: Lipids were separated on a C18 reverse-phase column (Waters Acquity CSH, 2.1 × 100 mm, 1.7 µm) using a binary gradient (mobile phase A: acetonitrile:water 6:4 v/v; mobile phase B: isopropanol:acetonitrile 9:1 v/v; both containing 10 mM ammonium formate and 0.1% formic acid), at 0.26 mL/min with the column oven at 60°C. The gradient was as follows: 0−1.5 min isocratic elution with 32% B; from 1.5 to 4 min increase to 45% B, from 4 to 5 min increase to 52% B, from 5 to 8 min to 58% B, from 8 to 11 min to 66% B, from 11 to 14 min to 70% B, from 14 to 18 min to 75% B, from 18 to 21 min to 97% B, during 21 to 25 min 97% B is maintained; from 25−25.1 min solvent B was decreased to 32% and then maintained for another 4.9 min for column re-equilibration (Hu et al. 2008 J Proteome Res , 7(11), https://doi.org/10.1021/pr800373m ). Data were acquired on a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer (ThermoFisher) with a heated electrospray ionization source, in both positive (spray voltage 4.0 kV) and negative (3.5 kV) ion mode, using full-scan/data-dependent MS2 acquisition (full-scan resolution 70,000 FWHM, scan range m/z 200–1,500, top 10 data-dependent ions per cycle, normalized stepped collision energy 15/27 eV, MS2 resolution 17,500). Mass calibration was performed in both ionization modes prior to analysis. Processing note: These are the original instrument .raw files prior to any peak picking, alignment, or annotation. They are intended to be processed through MS-DIAL 5 by the end user (recommended starting parameters: minimum peak height 1×10⁴ cps, MS1 tolerance 0.01 Da, MS2 tolerance 0.025 Da, minimum identification score 50%, retention time alignment tolerance 0.5 min), and are provided so that users of LipiRich can practise the full workflow starting from raw instrument output, or reprocess with their own MS-DIAL parameters. MS-DIAL parameter files and ISTD as msp libraries are provided on GitHub File contents: chow_13_pos, chow_6_pos, chow_4_pos, chow_7_pos, chow_5_pos, c
items.title: Untargeted LC-MS lipidomics of mouse liver from chow, lard, and fish oil-fed C57BL/6 mice: demonstration dataset for LipiRich

items.summary: A provenance analysis for a query evaluation or a model checking computation extracts information on how its result depends on the atomic facts of the model or database. Traditional work on data provenance was, to a large extent, restricted to positive query languages or the negation-free fragment of first-order logic and showed how provenance abstractions can be usefully described as elements of commutative semirings -- most generally as multivariate polynomials with positive integer coefficients. We describe and evaluate here a provenance approach for dealing with negation, based on quotient semirings of polynomials with dual indeterminates. This not only provides a semiring provenance analysis for full first-order logic (and other logics and query languages with negation) but also permits a reverse provenance analysis, i.e., finding models that satisfy various properties under given provenance tracking assumptions. We describe the potential for applications to explaining missing query answers or failures of integrity constraints, and to using these explanations for computing repairs. This approach also is the basis of a systematic study of semiring semantics in a broad logical context.
items.title: Provenance Analysis and Semiring Semantics for First-Order Logic

items.summary: This record contains the preprint paper "LOST IN THE PDFS: CONTEXT DEGRADATION AND PARAMETRIC HALLUCINATIONS IN LLM UIS" , authored by Gabriele D’Iorio (University of Naples Parthenope).  The study investigates the structural limitations and operational vulnerabilities of commercial web-based Large Language Model (LLM) interfaces when handling long, multi-document sequential workflows in educational contexts. Abstract: The growing use of LLMs for educational purposes, especially by inexperienced users, inevitably leads to LLMs hallucinating and making mistakes. This study presents an experiment using the web version of Gemini (Pro Standard and Flash Standard modes) to simulate a numerical analysis class covering three topics (interpolation, piecewise interpolation, and approximation), each in a separate PDF. This study is subdivided into two scenarios created to evaluate how the LLM responded and, above all, to see how long it took to hallucinate or suffer from context degradation. The results demonstrate the failure of both scenarios due to context degradation. Despite large theoretical context windows, sudden attachment truncation in the web UI forces the model to rely on its parametric memory, leading to severe hallucinations and sycophantic behavior. Key Topics Covered: - Context Degradation & "Lost in the Middle" Phenomenon: Analysis of how LLMs lose retrieval accuracy in prolonged sessions. - Parametric Hallucinations: How models compensate for context loss by fabricating details from pre-training data. - Document Parsing Challenges: Visual layout issues in standard Web UIs. - Experimental Evaluation: A comparative analysis of a single-chat setup (Scenario A) versus a dual-agent/tutor setup (Scenario B). Data Availability: The comprehensive dataset, interaction logs, prompt configurations, and Python scripts used for token counting are openly accessible in the project’s GitHub repository at: https://github.com/gabpolymath/lost_in_the_pdfs/
items.title: Lost in the PDFs: Context Degradation and Parametric Hallucinations in LLM UIs

items.summary: Generative AI is reshaping how research software is developed. Tools and patterns ranging from “vibe coding” through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and autonomous agents now offer compelling productivity gains, but their adoption in scientific computing surfaces failure modes that general-purpose evaluation does not catch: silent unit conversions, violated conservation laws, hallucinated physics, loss of numerical precision, and quietly broken reproducibility. These failures share a signature: nothing visible goes wrong. The AI ecosystem itself is moving fast, leaving RSEs to make consequential integration decisions with little shared vocabulary or principled guidance. This talk introduces Scientific Agentic Engineering , the central contribution of an in-progress 2026 Better Scientific Software (BSSw) Fellowship: a tool-agnostic methodology for integrating AI agents into high-stakes scientific software workflows. The framework defines how agents, scientific skills, and MCP servers should be structured around validation loops, explicit human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and domain-specific safeguards. Every task moves through a short workflow (frame, plan and critique, implement, verify), with decisions recorded throughout, and the framework maps each documented failure mode to the stage where it is cheapest to catch. The intent is not to recommend any particular AI tool but to articulate foundational concepts that remain valid as the underlying technology changes. I will share three artifacts from the fellowship: The Framework (published July 2026). Shared vocabulary, its principles and workflow, structural guidance on where safeguards live, and a pattern catalog of named practices, each tied to the failure it counters. The Reference Workflow. A structured exercise in which RSEs use AI tools to build a small weather-model error-statistics application, applying the framework to avoid the failure modes it documents. The Community Repository. A curated starter set of scientific MCP server templates, agent skills such as unit checkers and conservation-law validators, and agent configuration examples, designed to be starting points for the community to adapt to a variety of scientific domains. These artifacts are by design community resources, and broader adoption is the explicit aim of the remaining milestones, which include an interactive online tutorial series comparing purpose-built scientific agents with general-purpose tools, a recorded live workshop published for asynchronous access, and a BSSw.io blog post directing the community to the project’s resources. This work engages the conference theme directly by advancing AI-assisted scientific software development from ad-hoc experimentation toward a disciplined, transferable engineering practice.
items.title: Scientific Agentic Engineering: A Framework for Reliable AI Agents in Research Software

items.summary: VERSION 3 (2026-09-12) — Validity annotations, corrected re-analysis, and withdrawal of the associated preprint. Research materials retained. The preprint this record accompanied (EcoEvoRxiv, DOI 10.32942/X2DD40) is being withdrawn at the author's request because its central conclusions are not supported (withdrawal requested 12 September 2026; this sentence will be updated when the notice is posted). The manuscript was rejected by Journal of Molecular Evolution on 9 September 2026; the reviewer's comment on the imposed species-tree topology prompted the re-analysis. Provenance of this record: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21344531 was reserved in July 2026 for a planned version 2 that was never published (the upload did not complete). It was first published on 12 September 2026 as version 3. The only earlier public version is version 1 (10.5281/zenodo.21094823, 1 July 2026); every file of version 1, and of the unpublished version-2 package, is contained unchanged inside the version-3 archive (see validity_manifest.csv). The DOI that represents all versions and always resolves to the latest one is 10.5281/zenodo.21094822. (The README inside the archive calls 10.5281/zenodo.21094823 the concept DOI; that number denotes version 1.) Re-analysis (11 September 2026) identified: a rooted-tree input to PAML codeml that made root-adjacent branch estimates non-identifiable and inflated the headline statistic (88.6 % → 71.5 % with unrooted trees; 845 → 1,374 orthogroups after QC); imposed species and gene-tree topologies that are rejected by the data themselves (Astrephomene is sister to Volvocaceae, support 100/100); pooling of two independent origins of multicellularity that carry different results (Goniaceae+Volvocaceae 73 %, Tetrabaenaceae 48 %); and a terminal-branch-length gradient that confounds evolutionary rate with time since each lineage's last sampled split (differentiated lineages are not slower than their undifferentiated sister clades in 263 public genes, and there is no cell-number gradient across 57 species: PGLS β = −0.04, P = 0.69). Supplementary Tables S5b/S5c contained unfinished placeholders. items.summary: This record contains the preprint paper "LOST IN THE PDFS: CONTEXT DEGRADATION AND PARAMETRIC HALLUCINATIONS IN LLM UIS" , authored by Gabriele D’Iorio (University of Naples Parthenope).  The study investigates the structural limitations and operational vulnerabilities of commercial web-based Large Language Model (LLM) interfaces when handling long, multi-document sequential workflows in educational contexts. Abstract: The growing use of LLMs for educational purposes, especially by inexperienced users, inevitably leads to LLMs hallucinating and making mistakes. This study presents an experiment using the web version of Gemini (Pro Standard and Flash Standard modes) to simulate a numerical analysis class covering three topics (interpolation, piecewise interpolation, and approximation), each in a separate PDF. This study is subdivided into two scenarios created to evaluate how the LLM responded and, above all, to see how long it took to hallucinate or suffer from context degradation. The results demonstrate the failure of both scenarios due to context degradation. Despite large theoretical context windows, sudden attachment truncation in the web UI forces the model to rely on its parametric memory, leading to severe hallucinations and sycophantic behavior. Key Topics Covered: - Context Degradation & "Lost in the Middle" Phenomenon: Analysis of how LLMs lose retrieval accuracy in prolonged sessions. - Parametric Hallucinations: How models compensate for context loss by fabricating details from pre-training data. - Document Parsing Challenges: Visual layout issues in standard Web UIs. - Experimental Evaluation: A comparative analysis of a single-chat setup (Scenario A) versus a dual-agent/tutor setup (Scenario B). Data Availability: The comprehensive dataset, interaction logs, prompt configurations, and Python scripts used for token counting are openly accessible in the project’s GitHub repository at: https://github.com/gabpolymath/lost_in_the_pdfs/
items.title: Lost in the PDFs: Context Degradation and Parametric Hallucinations in LLM UIs

items.summary: 2.2.0 A minor version, not a patch: the change below alters what a default run leaves on disk. Nothing about your results, final outputs or logs changes, but a default that deletes files users previously got to keep is more than a patch. Changed Intermediate pfiles are now deleted as the run progresses, at defaults. Each QC step reads a genotype file and writes a new one — callrate reads your input and writes …_callrate , sex reads that and writes …_sex , and so on — so a ten-step run creates ten copies of your data. At GP2 release scale each copy is tens of GiB. Cleanup used to be skipped whenever warn_only was set, and warn-and-continue is the default , so at defaults every copy survived for the whole run. The only way to reclaim the disk was --no-warn , which also turns warn-and-continue into fail-fast — so you could not have both. That is a bad trade on a long run, where warn-and-continue exists precisely so an eight-hour job does not die on one recoverable step. The two flags no longer interfere: | | before | now | |---|---|---| | (default) | keeps every copy | deletes each copy once the next is written | | --full-output | keeps every copy | keeps every copy | | --no-warn | deletes + fail-fast | fail-fast only | | --no-warn --full-output | keeps + fail-fast | keeps + fail-fast | --full-output is now the only switch governing retention; --no-warn is purely failure policy. Peak disk during a run drops from roughly one working copy per step to one overall — on the round-19 full-GP2 run, ~98 GiB written against a ~50 GiB peak. If you relied on the old default to inspect intermediates, pass --full-output — it reproduces the previous behavior exactly. A failed step's input is still kept either way, so a broken run can still be examined.

items.summary: This dataset provides a harmonized global collection of river discharge (Q), suspended sediment concentration (SSC), and suspended sediment load (SSL) observations for source-traceable sediment-data analysis and model evaluation. It integrates observations from multiple monitoring networks, regional datasets, literature compilations, and satellite-derived products, with standardized metadata, coordinates, temporal information, variable definitions, and units. Missing sediment variables are derived where appropriate, gauge locations are linked to MERIT-Basins river reaches and upstream drainage units, and variable-level quality flags are provided to distinguish good, derived, suspect, bad, and missing values. Provenance information is preserved so that released records can be traced to their contributing source stations and datasets. The release consists of three complementary components. The main station-reference component contains 7,135 unique stations and 2,997,121 records from 17 source datasets spanning 1912–2025, distributed as separate daily, monthly, and annual station-by-time NetCDF products according to source-reported temporal support. The climatology auxiliary component contains 1,361 stations from five sources and provides long-term or climatological Q, SSC, and SSL information, with reported source coverage extending from 1884 to 2017. The satellite-derived auxiliary component contains 38,550 locations and 16,478,276 records from three source datasets spanning 1984–2020 and provides complementary spatial coverage, mainly for SSC. The archive includes the daily, monthly, and annual NetCDF products; climatology and satellite-derived auxiliary NetCDF products and their accompanying query catalogues; station, source-station, and source-dataset catalogues; and dataset documentation. The catalogues preserve station-level and source-level provenance and support station screening, source tracing, and reproducible use of the released products. The main station-reference component is intended for station-level time-series extraction, source-traceable benchmarking, and evaluation of hydrological, river-routing, erosion, sediment-transport, and land-surface models. The climatology and satellite-derived components provide complementary long-term and spatial context and should not be treated as direct substitutes for the time-resolved station-reference products. Daily, monthly, and annual products represent different temporal support and should be selected according to the requirements of each analysis rather than combined without accounting for observation coverage. This dataset is intended as a reusable and extensible community resource. Future releases may incorporate additional observations and improvements to the harmonization and integration framework while preserving versioned releases for reproducibility.
items.title: A Harmonized Global Station-Reference Dataset of River Discharge, Suspended Sediment Concentration, and Suspended Sediment Load

items.summary: Automated risk decisions increasingly depend on probabilistic assessments transmitted across organisational and computational boundaries. A probability estimate may remain numerically intact while losing the contextual information required to evaluate its evidentiary dependence — a condition we term Provenance Loss . We introduce Orphaned Inference — a probabilistic output P ( H | E ) that propagates downstream after its contextual qualification is stripped at a transmission boundary — and show that when downstream agents continue scalar-posterior updating using marginal likelihood ratios, the resulting propagation is equivalent to a Na ̈ıve-Bayes-style independence approximation over the correlated evidence sequence. This double-counts the shared environmental signal, producing Directional Context Amplification , quantified by the Cumulative Provenance Amplification (CPA n ) metric. Under environmental context drift ( C 0 → C 1 ), accumulated phantom certainty persists into the post-shift regime as Post-Shift Epistemic Persistence , driving the mean absolute posterior error close to 1 in true-negative states ( H = 0) during the pre-shift period. In risk-analysis terms, provenance loss separates the numerical value of a risk estimate from the evidentiary conditions under which it remains decision-valid: downstream decision makers may receive an apparently precise probability whose effective evidentiary weight is substantially overstated. A Monte Carlo simulation ( N = 5 , 000 trials, n = 15 agent chain) demonstrates the predicted cascade under the specified parameter regime and documents monotone growth of CPA n across sampled correlation values ρ ∈ { 0 , . . . , 0 . 8 } . We propose three provenance-aware risk-control safeguards and discuss their governance trade-offs.
items.title: Orphaned Inferences in Automated Risk Hierarchies: Na ̈ıve Bayes Amplification under Provenance Loss

items.summary: This repository contains two LC–MS/MS raw data files (and .mgf versions if needed), associated search parameters, and curated FASTA databases generated from purified fibrinogen clots crosslinked by endogenous FXIIIa or recombinant transglutaminase 2 (TG2). These samples represent a controlled benchmark system for evaluating crosslink-mass spectrometry (XL-MS) software performance on non-cleavable enzymatic Q–K isopeptide bonds. items.summary: Abstract Background  Thyroid dysfunction is one of the most common endocrine disorders affecting metabolic activity, psychological well-being, and gastrointestinal function.(1,2) Patients frequently experience elevated thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels, stress, bloating, impaired digestion, reduced metabolic efficiency, and decreased quality of life. Although conventional treatment effectively restores thyroid hormone balance in many patients, complementary therapeutic interventions are increasingly being explored to improve overall clinical outcomes and patient-reported health status.  Aim  To evaluate the effect of a Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid on thyroid function, perceived stress, gastrointestinal symptoms, and participant-reported global improvement among adults with thyroid dysfunction.  Materials and Methods:  A prospective, single-arm interventional clinical study was conducted involving  22 adult participants  diagnosed with thyroid dysfunction. Baseline demographic characteristics including age, body weight, height, and body mass index (BMI) were recorded. Clinical assessments included serum thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), perceived stress score (0–40 scale), gastrointestinal symptoms related to bloating, digestion, and metabolism, and Participant Global Impression of Change (PGIC). All parameters were assessed before and after the intervention. The composition of the study formulation will be described separately. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate descriptive and inferential statistical methods, and statistical significance was considered at  p  < 0.05.  Results:  The intervention demonstrated an overall improvement in multiple clinical outcomes. Mean serum TSH decreased from  10.27 to 3.77 mIU/L , while mean perceived stress scores decreased from  20.45 to 13.18 . Improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms and PGIC scores was observed in the majority of participants. Perceived stress scores decreased in a substantial proportion of participants, indicating improvement in psychological well-being. Gastrointestinal symptoms such as bloating and impaired digestion improved from mild or moderate severity to normal or minimal symptoms in the majority of cases. Participant-reported outcomes also demonstrated favorable changes, with PGIC scores increasing in most participants, suggesting meaningful overall clinical improvement. The intervention was generally well tolerated, and no serious adverse events were documented during the study period.  Conclusion:  The findings of this prospective clinical study suggest that the investigated Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid may contribute to improved thyroid function, reduction in perceived stress, better gastrointestinal health, and enhanced patient-reported quality of life in adults with thyroid dysfunction. These preliminary findings support the potential role of the formulation as a complementary therapeutic option. Larger randomized controlled clinical trials with extended follow-up are warranted to confirm these observations and establish long-term efficacy and safety.   Keywords: Thyroid Dysfunction; Thyroid Stimulating Hormone; TSH; Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid; Teacurry Thyroid Tea; Teacurry; Thyroid Tea; Herbal Tea for Thyroid; Complementary ##plugin
items.title: Effect of a Plant-Based Herbal Tea Formulation "Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid" on Thyroid Function, TSH Levels, Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Participant-Reported Global Improvement in Adults with Thyroid Dysfunction: Real-World Evidence Clinical Study

items.summary: Background: Surface roughness is an important characteristic of resin composite restorations and may be influenced by material composition and finishing and polishing procedures. Objective: To evaluate changes in surface roughness (Ra) of nanofilled, nanohybrid, and microhybrid resin composites after sequential finishing and polishing and to compare their final surface roughness. Materials and Methods: S ixty disc-shaped specimens (8 mm × 2 mm; shade A2) were fabricated using Filtek Z350 XT, IPS Empress Direct, and Filtek Z250 (n = 20 per material). Fifteen specimens per material underwent a standardized finishing and polishing protocol using fine- and extra-fine-grit diamond burs followed by sequential Sof-Lex discs, while five specimens per material remained untreated as controls. Surface roughness was measured using a Mitutoyo SJ-210 contact profilometer at baseline   and after the intervention. Because specimen-level identification was not preserved between measurement sessions, baseline and final measurements were analyzed as independent observations using independent-samples t-tests, with Welch’s correction when required. Final Ra values among materials were compared using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey HSD tests (α = 0.05). Results: All three experimental composites showed statistically significant increases in Ra after finishing and polishing (all p < 0.001), whereas no statistically significant changes were observed in the untreated controls (all p > 0.05). Mean Ra increased from 0.085 to 0.181 μm for IPS Empress Direct, from 0.111 to 0.186 μm for Filtek Z350 XT, and from 0.122 to 0.195 μm for Filtek Z250. Final Ra values did not differ significantly among the three materials (F(2,42) = 0.559, p = 0.576). Conclusions: Sequential finishing and polishing significantly increased surface roughness relative to the strip-polymerized baseline surfaces of all three resin composites, without statistically significant differences in final Ra among the materials. The final mean Ra values remained below the predefined 0.2 μm surface-roughness threshold. Under the experimental conditions evaluated, post-polishing surface roughness could not be predicted solely on the basis of nanofilled, nanohybrid, or microhybrid filler classification.
items.title: Surface Roughness of Nanofilled, Nanohybrid, and Microhy-brid Resin Composites After Sequential Finishing and Polish-ing: An In Vitro Comparative Study

items.summary: A 0.1° monthly and daily terrestrial water storage anomaly (TWSA) product for the Ganga (Ganges) River Basin, 2000–2025 , together with the source code, the inputs, and the full evaluation record that produced it. GRACE and GRACE-FO JPL RL06 mascons are spatially downscaled by fitting a predictor–TWSA relation across mascons; every mascon's area-weighted aggregate is then forced back onto the observed value. The monthly field is disaggregated to daily under an exact monthly constraint, its within-month shape supplied by the ERA5-Land water balance with nothing fitted at the daily scale. Per-pixel uncertainty is reported as four separate terms rather than one number, because only some of them are measurable against an observation. What changed in v1.0.1, and what did not. The data are unchanged. The three product netCDFs, the monthly and daily COGs, the trend field and every input and intermediate archive are the same files already in this record — if you have them, there is nothing to download again, and any analysis built on v1.0.0 stands. Four files change, all of them code or documentation: grace-grb-1.0.1.zip , the source at the new tag, which adds main/trend_regions.py and the scripts behind three manuscript figures; evaluation_tables.zip , which gains trend_by_region.csv ; figures.zip , which gains those three plates; and DATA_README.md . The version exists for reproducibility rather than revision: the regional trend figures quoted in the paper were computed from a region definition that had never been committed, so a reader holding the archived trend field could not reproduce them. That definition is now in the archive, it is checked to partition the basin, and the paper cites this version. What is imposed and what is learned. Each mascon's level and linear trend are taken from GRACE rather than learned from the predictors — the secular signal here is groundwater abstraction, and no reanalysis simulates pumping. Only the sub-mascon anomaly is modelled, from 78 predictor features built on ERA5-Land and nine covariates, seven of them static and two annual cropland fractions held constant after 2022. Mass conservation then forces every mascon mean back onto the observation by a minimum-norm correction. Agreement with GRACE at mascon scale is therefore arithmetic, not evidence of skill : the basin mean of this product reproduces the GRACE basin mean at r = 1.00000, RMSE 0.27 mm. We state that plainly so it is not mistaken for validation. Held-out performance. Skill is reported only where it can be measured — at spatial units the model never saw, at times it never saw, and against an independent observation. Spatial (leave-one-mascon-out, 19 folds with a neighbour buffer): RMSE 88.2 mm, R² 0.638, NSE 0.635 over 83,309 held-out cell-months. Cluster bootstrap over mascons (2,000 resamples): RMSE 82.1–95.1 mm, R² 0.580–0.694. Temporal (whole months held out): interior gap-filling RMSE 71.7 mm (R² 0.775); scattered months 74.5 mm (0.713), a random split and so optimistic — each withheld month keeps its neighbours in training; out-of-record extrapolation 91.1 mm (0.730) . The last is the regime the post-2024 months live in. Independent (656 quality-controlled CGWB dug wells): at basin scale the downscaled field reaches r = 0.814, RMSE 57.0 mm against a bilinear-interpolation baseline at r = 0.742, RMSE 73.1 mm. Skill is strongly scale-dependent: median R² is 0.48 per mascon but 0.19 per well, and NSE exceeds zero at only 168 of 656 wells. Neither side is ground truth — a well is a point head times an estimated specific yield, the product a 0.1° cell from a 3° mascon — so the scale dependence is reported as the result rather than a single pooled number.
